2610.12306.title: A Structural Theory of Cognitive Representation and Problem Solving,Contexts, Invariance, and the Knowledge Space
2610.12306.paper_summary: Learning and problem solving depend critically on the structure of internal representations. While many modern data-driven artificial systems achieve strong predictive performance, their learned representations often lack explicit structure for expressing abstraction, invariance, and task-relevant regularities. We propose a minimal structural framework in which representational operations relevant to problem solving, such as context formation, invariance recognition, representative selection, abstraction, and procedural reuse, are made explicit. The central notion is that of a \emph{context}, formalized as a partition of a subset of an underlying state space, which fixes the distinctions, granularity, and form in which a problem can be posed. Within this setting, invariance recognition and representative selection are treated as fundamental representational operations. The framework is realized as a Knowledge Space composed of two coupled graph structures: a Concept Graph that hosts constructed and refined concepts, and a Procedure Graph that encodes typed operations over representations. Together, these structures provide a minimal cognitive-representational algebra for operating on representations without assuming sophisticated inference, learning, control, perception, or motor mechanisms. Using simple illustrative examples and a finite weak-solver demonstration, we show that appropriate representational organization can simplify the form and scope of admissible regularities, even when problem solving is carried out by a fixed and limited solver. The contribution of the paper is structural rather than algorithmic: it identifies representational prerequisites for abstraction, invariance, and procedural reuse in problem solving, and states explicit success and failure conditions for the weak-solver setting.
2610.12306.paper_summary_zh: 學習和問題解決在很大程度上依賴於內部表徵的結構。雖然許多現代數據驅動的人工系統在預測性能上表現出色，但它們所學習的表徵往往缺乏明確的結構來表達抽象性、不變性和與任務相關的規律。我們提出了一個最小結構框架，其中與問題解決相關的表徵操作，如上下文形成、不變性識別、代表性選擇、抽象和程序重用，都被明確化。核心概念是\emph{上下文}，它被形式化為基礎狀態空間子集的劃分，這固定了問題可以提出的區分、粒度和形式。在這個設置中，不變性識別和代表性選擇被視為基本的表徵操作。該框架實現為一個知識空間，由兩個耦合的圖結構組成：一個概念圖，承載構建和精煉的概念，以及一個程序圖，編碼對表徵的類型操作。這些結構共同提供了一個最小的認知-表徵代數，用於操作表徵，而不假設複雜的推理、學習、控制、感知或運動機制。通過簡單的示例和有限的弱解算器演示，我們展示了適當的表徵組織可以簡化可接受規律的形式和範圍，即使問題解決是由固定和有限的解算器進行的。本文的貢獻是結構性的，而非算法性的：它確定了問題解決中抽象、不變性和程序重用的表徵前提，並明確陳述了弱解算器設置的成功和失敗條件。
